# The Second Half Guide

> Smart, practical information for people roughly 55-70 navigating the financial and lifestyle transition into retirement. Every dollar amount, age threshold and deadline is checked against the agency that publishes it, and the sources are listed at the foot of each article.

Published by Edward Silva. Not financial, legal, medical or tax advice; this is a publisher, not an advisor. Figures are stated for the year named on the page and change annually. Every page is listed in https://thesecondhalfguide.com/sitemap.xml.

## Medicare & health insurance
- [Travel insurance after 60: what are you actually buying?](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/travel-insurance): It gets sold as one checkbox at the end of a booking. It’s at least four different products — and the one most people over 65 need isn’t the one they think.
- [The Medicare Part B drug test that starts in 2027, and who is in it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/globe-part-b-drugs): CMS finalized GLOBE, a mandatory Part B drug pricing test for Original Medicare patients in randomly chosen areas. Who is in it, when it starts, the lawsuit.
- [The 2027 Medicare plan numbers, and what an average can’t tell you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-2027-costs): CMS projects lower 2027 Medicare Advantage premiums, a Part D deductible of up to $700 and a $2,400 cap. What an average can't tell you about your plan.
- [Medicare’s sales rules loosen on October 1](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-marketing-rules-2026): Medicare's sales rules loosen October 1 -- shorter call recordings, no SOA wait. What changed, and the two protections that did not.
- [The Medicare Advantage debit card rule arriving in 2027](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/ma-flex-card-2027): Starting in 2027, Medicare Advantage debit cards check purchases in real time and unused balances no longer roll into the next year. What changed.
- [The next round of Medicare drug discounts arrives in January](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/drug-negotiation-2027): CMS finalized new Medicare drug prices months ago, including a 71% cut on Ozempic and Wegovy. Effective January 1 -- what that means, and does not, for you.
- [More Medicare Advantage plans are disappearing for 2027](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/ma-plan-exits-2027): Humana, UnitedHealthcare and Molina are exiting Medicare Advantage markets for 2027, hundreds of thousands of members combined. What happens if yours is one.
- [The Medicare letter arriving in September, and why it’s worth reading](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/anoc-letter): Every Medicare Advantage and Part D plan must mail its Annual Notice of Change by September 30. What it says, and the 2027 numbers now confirmed.
- [The $2,100 drug cap: real protection, narrower than it sounds](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/drug-cap): Part D prescription costs now have a hard annual ceiling of $2,100. A genuinely big change — and “out-of-pocket cap” is doing a lot of work.
- [Open enrollment: what the 15 October window is actually for](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/open-enrollment): Your plan is allowed to change its costs, its drug list and its doctors every January. Fall is the only time most people can respond — and most don’t.
- [The other Medicare enrollment window, in January](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-advantage-oep): A second Medicare enrollment window opens every January, separate from fall’s AEP — but only for people already on Medicare Advantage, and only once.
- [The COBRA-to-Medicare trap](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/cobra-medicare-trap): COBRA keeps your health plan going after a job ends, but it isn’t creditable coverage for Medicare Part B — missing that risks a permanent penalty.
- [The HSA rule that can cost you a 6% tax at 65](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/hsa-medicare-timing): Still working past 65 with an HSA? Enrolling in Medicare later can retroactively tax contributions already made. The 6-month rule that avoids the 6% penalty.
- [The ACA subsidy cliff is back in 2026](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/aca-subsidy-cliff): The enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025. What that means for marketplace premiums in 2026, and where the subsidy cliff now sits.
- [Long-term care: the numbers, before the sales pitch](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/long-term-care): What long-term care actually costs in 2026, who pays for it, and what insurance does and does not do. One of the largest risks in retirement.
- [The free Medicare visit that isn’t a physical](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/wellness-visit): You get one every year at no cost. It is not a physical, which is the source of most of the confusion — and of most of the surprise bills.
- [What Medicare doesn’t cover](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-gaps): What Medicare does not cover: teeth, eyes, ears, and the very large one most people do not discover until a parent needs it. Worth knowing early.
- [Advantage or Original: what actually differs](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/advantage-vs-original): Medicare Advantage or Original Medicare: what each one is, how the money works, and the one decision that gets much harder to reverse later on.
- [The Medicare deadline that never forgives you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-enrollment): Miss your Medicare enrollment window without the right coverage and you pay a surcharge every month for life. The seven months that decide it.
- [CMS canceled 760,000 Marketplace enrollments over fraud concerns](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/aca-unauthorized-enrollment): CMS canceled 315,000 Marketplace enrollments covering 760,000 people over fraud concerns. How to check whether your own coverage was affected.

## Money & the tax year
- [Should you file for Social Security at 62? Here's what the math actually says](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/social-security-62): Filing for Social Security at 62 cuts your benefit permanently. The arithmetic — the reduction, the break-even, and when filing early still wins.
- [The property tax break you might already qualify for](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/property-tax): Most states reduce, freeze or defer property taxes at a certain age. Almost none apply it automatically, and the age is lower than people assume.
- [The 2027 Social Security COLA isn’t official yet](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/cola-2027-estimate): Trackers estimate the 2027 Social Security COLA at 3.4%-3.6%, but nothing is official until SSA announces it in mid-October. What decides it.
- [The COLA: why a raise doesn’t feel like one](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/cola): Social Security rose 2.8% for 2026. For an average retired worker on the standard Part B premium, Medicare took back about a third before it arrived.
- [Locked out of your Social Security account](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/social-security-login): Your old Social Security username and password no longer work. Nothing went wrong — the sign-in system changed, and getting back in takes 20 minutes.
- [The pension rule that cut your Social Security is gone](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/wep-gpo-repeal): WEP and GPO cut the Social Security of teachers, firefighters and public employees for decades. Both were repealed, and many affected still don't know.
- [The widow’s penalty](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/widows-penalty): When one spouse dies, income falls and the tax brackets narrow at the same time. One of the harshest bits of arithmetic in retirement, rarely explained.
- [The six months that decide whether you can ever buy Medigap](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medigap-window): The one-time six-month Medigap window: when it starts, what guaranteed issue means, and what insurers may ask about your health once it closes.
- [Three nights in a hospital bed, and Medicare says you were never admitted](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/observation-status): Observation is a billing status, not a place. Why three hospital nights may not count toward Medicare's three-day rule, and the appeal opened in 2025.
- [The Medicare surcharge based on what you earned two years ago](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/irmaa): IRMAA 2026: the Medicare surcharge set by your income from two years ago. The thresholds, why it is a cliff not a slope, and the form that appeals it.
- [The Medicare help millions qualify for and never claim](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-savings): Four Medicare Savings Programs help with premiums and deductibles, plus Extra Help for drug costs. The 2026 income limits are higher than most assume.
- [Social Security’s automatic wage reporting, and what it still needs from you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/ssi-wage-reporting): SSA’s Payroll Information Exchange now reports many SSI and SSDI recipients’ wages automatically each month. What still has to be reported by hand.
- [Social Security’s fast track for a severe diagnosis](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/compassionate-allowances): SSA added 14 conditions to its Compassionate Allowances list on August 11, 2026, bringing the total to 314. How the disability fast track actually works.
- [The Social Security overpayment letter, and the deadline inside it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/overpayment-clawback): SSA can now withhold up to 50% of your monthly check to recover an overpayment. Two deadlines inside the letter — 30 and 60 days — decide when that starts.
- [When your 401(k) catch-up must go into Roth, and what changes in 2027](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/roth-catch-up): Since 2026, 401(k) catch-up contributions for workers 50+ over a prior-year wage threshold must be Roth. Who is covered, which wages count, what 2027 adds.
- [Social Security’s claiming ages are getting new names](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/claiming-age-clarity-act): Congress sent the President a bill renaming Social Security's early, full and delayed claiming ages. The new names, and why no age or dollar amount changes.
- [The four-year 401(k) catch-up window at 60–63](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/catch-up-60-63): For four calendar years only, ages 60–63, the 401(k) catch-up jumps to $11,250 instead of $8,000 — if your plan opts in, and if you know to ask.
- [Social Security spousal benefits: what you’re actually entitled to](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/spousal-benefits): Married or divorced, you may be owed a Social Security benefit based on a spouse’s record — up to half, not on top of your own. The rules that decide it.
- [What delaying Social Security actually adds to your check](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/delayed-retirement-credit): Waiting past full retirement age adds 8% a year to your Social Security check, up to 24% at 70. The published SSA rule, not a hidden bonus.
- [The Rule of 55: what it actually covers](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/rule-of-55): Leave a job at 55 or later and you may tap that employer’s 401(k) penalty-free. The IRS rule, the rollover trap that cancels it, and what still gets taxed.
- [The withdrawal the IRS requires, and the deadline that costs 25%](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/rmd-deadline): Required minimum distributions in 2026: the age by birth year, the first-year trap, the 25% penalty, and the charitable route that skips the tax.
- [The senior deduction ends after 2028](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/senior-deduction-sunset): The $6,000 senior deduction applies to tax years 2025 through 2028 and then ends. What that means for timing a conversion or a sale.
- [“No tax on Social Security”: what the law actually did](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/no-tax-on-social-security): The 2025 law created a $6,000 deduction for people over 65. It did not change how Social Security is taxed — those thresholds are frozen since 1984.
- [What someone over 65 can actually deduct in 2026](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/standard-deduction-65): Three separate deductions stack for someone over 65 in 2026: the base, the age-65 addition, and the new $6,000. Together, more than most expect.
- [The $75,000 line, and what the senior deduction is worth above it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/senior-deduction-phaseout): The $6,000 senior deduction shrinks by six cents per dollar above $75,000 single or $150,000 joint, and reaches zero at $175,000. The arithmetic.
- [The new $6,000 senior deduction, explained](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/senior-deduction): The new $6,000 senior deduction for people 65 and over — temporary, income-limited, and widely misdescribed as “no tax on Social Security.”

## Paperwork that matters
- [Power of attorney: the document for while you’re still here](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/power-of-attorney): A will handles what happens after you die. It does nothing for the far more likely problem — being alive, and temporarily unable to sign anything.
- [Who gets your digital life when you die?](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/digital-estate): Photographs, bills and password resets now live behind a login — and a password is not the same as permission. What an executor can actually reach.
- [Your beneficiary form may outrank your will](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/beneficiary-form): A will is the document everyone has heard of. For a lot of households, it isn’t the one that decides where the largest accounts go.

## Scam & fraud protection
- [The phone call that empties bank accounts — and the one sentence that stops it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/bank-imposter-scam): How the bank impostor call works, why it defeats careful people, and the one sentence that stops it — plus what to do if one has already reached you.
- [Romance scams after 55: intelligence was never the issue](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/romance-scams): The strongest ones don’t begin with a request for money. They begin with six months of someone remembering your grandchildren’s names.
- [When the voice really does sound like your grandchild](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/voice-cloning): The grandparent scam had one reliable flaw: the caller never sounded right. Voice cloning removed it. What still works has nothing to do with the voice.
- [Why your phone rings more in October](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/enrollment-scams): Open enrollment is the one season when unsolicited Medicare contact feels normal. That is what makes it the most profitable weeks of the fraud year.
- [When the scammer sends someone to your door](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/gold-courier-scam): The FBI logged about 725 gold-courier frauds in 2025, with $311.8 million lost and 98% of it by people over 60. It ends with a stranger at your door.
- [The parking meter QR code might not be the real one](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/qr-parking-scam): The FTC warns scammers are sticking fake QR codes over real ones on parking meters. How the trick works, and the check that stops it.
- [The new Medicare card scam, and the real reissue behind it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-card-scam): CMS reissued about 1.3 million Medicare numbers this spring as a fraud-prevention measure. Scammers quickly turned the real reissue into a new phone script.
- [The five-minute rule: why scammers need you to act right now](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/five-minute-rule): Modern fraud isn’t an intelligence test. It’s an attack on your decision time — which is why one boring habit beats memorising every scam.
- [The medical equipment fraud crackdown, and what to check on your own statement](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medical-equipment-fraud): CMS barred 11 equipment suppliers tied to $3.4 billion in suspected fraudulent billing. What to actually check on your own Medicare statement.
- [The Medicare website that is really an ad](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/search-ad-scam): The FTC warns that paid search ads can imitate Medicare.gov before open enrollment. How to spot a paid result and where the official site and phone line are.

## Aging in place
- [Most states will let you take college classes free after 60](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/free-college): Most states let older residents take public-college courses free or cheaply. Rules vary by state, campus, age, and whether you audit or take credit.
- [Hearing aids: what the over-the-counter rule actually changed](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/hearing-aids): For decades a pair cost as much as a used car and required an audiologist. Since 2022 you can buy them off a shelf — and the price floor fell through.
- [The driving conversation](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/driving): Age alone is a poor predictor of who should stop driving. The specific, checkable things that are better ones — and the road in between the two.
- [Downsizing: the arithmetic people skip](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/downsizing-math): Selling a big house and buying a small one may free up less than you think. The costs that decide it are the ones nobody puts in the spreadsheet.
- [Pickleball is sending more people to the ER than it used to](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/pickleball-injuries): Pickleball ER visits nearly quadrupled since 2018, and adults 50+ are most of them. The numbers, and what actually reduces the injury risk.
- [Falls: the numbers, and what actually reduces them](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/falls): More than one in four older adults falls each year and fall deaths are up 51% in a decade. The best-supported prevention costs nothing at all.
- [Aging in place: staying home is a goal, not a plan](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/aging-in-place): “I’m never leaving this house” sounds like a decision about a house. It’s mostly a decision about stairs, driving, and who lives near enough to help.

## Travel & discounts
- [ETIAS: the EU travel authorization that isn’t live yet](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/etias): ETIAS, Europe's €20 travel authorization, has no start date, and sites charging for it aren't the EU. What actually applies to Americans at the border now.
- [Portugal’s retirement visa income rule just went up again](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/portugal-d7-visa): Portugal ties its D7 retirement visa income floor to the minimum wage, which rose again for 2026. What changed, and why renewals get checked again.
- [Which senior travel discounts still actually exist in 2026](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/senior-travel-discounts): Amtrak still publishes a clear 10% senior discount. The major airlines do not -- what still exists, carrier by carrier, and how to actually check.
- [The fee-free days don’t do anything for you if you have the Senior Pass](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/parks-fee-free-days): The 2026 fee-free days now exclude nonresidents, and two prior holidays dropped off the list. What it means if you already have the Senior Pass.
- [The “go-go years” are real, but they’re not a deadline](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/go-go-years): Retirement planners split later life into go-go, slow-go and no-go. There’s something to it — and it has quietly turned a lot of 60s into a countdown clock.
- [Is the National Parks Senior Pass still one of America’s best deals?](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/parks-pass): $80 for life, starting at 62. The headline is as good as it sounds — but the word “parks” misleads people about what they’re actually buying.
- [The vaccine schedule nobody hands you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/vaccine-ages): Children get a schedule on a card. Adults get nothing — despite several vaccines now starting at 50, and most of them costing nothing on Medicare.
- [Skip-gen travel: grandparents and grandkids, no parents](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/skip-gen-travel): Grandparents plan 75% of skip-gen trips and pay for 84% of them. What the survey shows, and the consent paperwork that can stop a trip at the border.
- [The big trip, done right](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/the-big-trip): Not where to go — you know where you want to go. The logistics that decide whether the trip you have been imagining for years actually works.
- [What happens if you get sick on a cruise](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/cruise-medical): There is a doctor on board, they bill you, and Medicare almost certainly does not apply. What shipboard care costs, and what evacuation can run to.
- [Flying with medications and medical equipment](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/travel-medications): Most of it is easier than people fear. One thing is a hard no, and a few require paperwork weeks in advance — which is the part that ruins trips.
- [The passport rules that turn people away at check-in](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/passport-traps): A valid passport is not always a usable one. The rule that catches people has nothing to do with the expiry date printed inside it.
- [The airport rule that went away, and what PreCheck still buys you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/airport-security): TSA ended the shoes-off rule for everyone in July 2025, deleting the one screening benefit of turning 75. What PreCheck and Global Entry still buy you.
- [The airport help you’re entitled to, and nobody mentions](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/airport-help): Wheelchairs, escorts through the terminal, help through security — all free and yours by law. Almost entirely unused, because nobody tells you.
- [55, 60, 62, 65: when does “senior” actually start?](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/senior-age): There is no senior birthday. About a dozen unrelated clocks — 50, 55, 59½, 62, 65, 67 — set by different institutions, and only some of them matter.

## Grandparenting & family
- [The Wednesday Letters](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/wednesday-letters): Fiction from The Second Half Guide: twenty-one years of Wednesday mornings at a small-town post office, and the letters that kept on arriving.
- [The grandparent 529 rule changed, and most families still don’t know it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/grandparent-529-fafsa): A federal rule change removed the FAFSA penalty on grandparent-paid 529 distributions -- but some private colleges use a form that still asks.
- [The new long-distance grandparent](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/long-distance): Living far from grandchildren changes the mechanics of closeness, not the closeness itself. What has to be built rather than simply absorbed.
- [Being available without being on call](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/on-call): Grandparenting can be the best thing about this decade. It can also become a job nobody remembers offering you, and that nobody remembers accepting.

## Reference
- [Approaching 60 and beyond: what actually changes, and what doesn't](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/approaching-60): What actually changes as you approach 60: the deadlines worth a calendar entry, the thresholds that matter, and the many that are only marketing.
- [The numbers worth keeping by the phone](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/numbers): The real phone numbers for Medicare, Social Security, fraud reporting and local help — checked, with hours, and printable for the kitchen drawer.
- [Why this site exists](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/about): Who writes The Second Half Guide, how it is funded, how the facts are checked, and the standards it holds itself to. Published by Edward Silva.

## Interactive tools
- [The Second Half Retirement Planner: Social Security 62 vs. 65 vs. 67](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/retirement-strategy-model): Privacy-first browser calculator comparing claiming ages, retirement savings, spending gaps, work earnings-test effects, couple combinations and Medicare timing.
